digest.component_or_area: inbound-probe dispatch chain and deletion-resurrection reconciliation
propositions: The (inbound, probe) dispatch chain has no live producer: differ._compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes only emits on jira_key-bearing local_state, but its sole caller run_differs passes a fetched Jira snapshot whose entries never carry jira_key

The deleted-vs-aged-out discrimination ADR-0028-para-2 relies on is already implemented live in outbound_differ._safe_get_issue and binding_walk.py, verified on real DC, making the inbound-probe arm architecturally redundant

Confirmed hard-deleted issues are currently resurrected eventually (after 3-pass grace period) via binding retirement and outbound-create, not immediately as ADR-0028-c244 documents, violating the documented same-pass guarantee

Prior art (Unito, Kubernetes) rejects resurrection of deliberately-deleted work items as wrong by default; the operator ruling forbids same-pass resurrection, making the implementation a defect to remove rather than restore

A never-bound local ticket must still get its outbound create, but a local ticket whose binding was retired on confirmed-404 must NOT be re-created, enforced by BindingStore.is_retired_local guard in outbound_differ

The dead chain removal (producer, dispatch, router, legacy test) and resurrection-path deletion expose a loose end: mutation._VALID_COMBINATIONS still admits (inbound, delete) and (inbound, probe) even though their handlers are gone, causing dispatch failures instead of early validation
